catalogRules.rule: One CatalogSnapshot per host, built once by the composition root (UAK1 layer LR) from static row providers. Nothing is registered, replaced or removed after construction.
The catalog is a set of separately typed tables T01-T09. There is no flat row enum spanning tables, no per-framework enum arm in a shared table type and no second registry beside the snapshot.

Registration carries no Any. Rows are concrete types; a frontend, backend or leg is a typed trait object of its capability trait. The confined carrier-parse downcast helpers stay outside registration.

No runtime plugin loading and no dynamic native ABI. An external contribution enters only as a validated T09 row admitted by XSDK1, which yields a new snapshot with a new identity; it never mutates a built snapshot.
Each table is ordered by the canonical encoding of its row key. The order rows were provided in, the order the composition root calls providers and hash-map iteration never decide table order.

Snapshot identity (VID0 I09) is the canonical tagged encoding of the ProfileSchemaEpoch and the semantic fields of every table in canonical order. Presentation fields (CR09) are excluded. It never includes provider order, admission options, workspace or project state, revisions, or process/backend identity (VID0 R14).

Duplicate-owner rejection: two rows with the same key in one table, two carrier rows claiming the same extension at the same precedence, two carrier rows sharing one editor language id, or a referenced id with no row fail construction with a typed error naming both owners. There is no last-wins or first-wins row.
Every carrier row has a frontend. A compiler backend row is optional; its absence is a normal state.
Presentation order is row data (T03 presentation rank), separate from canonical order. Generated mirrors render in presentation order; snapshot identity and dispatch never read it.

Kernel services, products and hosts select rows by typed id read from the snapshot or the DemandPlan. A display family, an adapter spelling or a file extension is never a dispatch or cache key (VID0 R03, UAK1 F04).
Admission and participation are not registration. Process flags, init options and editor settings never filter or re-mint the snapshot; selecting what runs belongs to the DemandPlan (DEM0, COX0).
Generated client mirrors are rendered only from snapshot rows, by one generator per mirror, and byte-pinned by a freshness test. A hand edit or a second source for the same bytes is forbidden.
Adding a family is a data change: new rows in the family's own module and regenerated mirrors. Neutral routing code needs no edit, branch or switch arm (the dormant row, RM09).

Conflicting claims between rows, static or contributed, resolve by a deterministic rule over row keys and declared relations, or yield a typed ambiguous or rejected outcome. First-loaded or fastest-returning never wins.

findings.finding: Admission composes a different catalog today: HostServices::composed filters both the capability catalog and the adapter registry by FrameworkOptions, so a Vue-only host has a smaller registration set. CR11 separates them; the observable Vue-only outcome moves to the DemandPlan.

Table order today is the frontend catalog's static order (composed_rows_keep_the_frontend_catalog_order). CR05 replaces it with canonical key order; CR09 keeps the generated mirrors' Vue-then-Svelte bytes through the presentation rank.

REG0's charter proposes CarrierGrammarConfig gaining a Framework(FrameworkCarrierKey) arm with pre-allocated keys, while UAK0 D01 has CPF1 replace the central enum with owner-local configs. Under CR02 a pre-allocated central arm per family would be a per-framework enum arm in a shared table type. REG0 must place its grammar keys in family row modules over the CPF1 shape.

The framework-surface result stores live on the registration rows (FrameworkRegistration.surface_store). A registration row must not own a result cache; D14 (TIF1) deletes the stores, and the T03 row carries no cache.
